scenario_text: Consider an ideal binary mixture distributed randomly over equivalent microscopic sites at thermal equilibrium. The sampled composition determines the configurational entropy per site through the multiplicity of distinguishable arrangements. The target is the dimensionless mixing entropy after removing composition-independent contributions. Energetic interactions and spatial correlations are held fixed at zero in the baseline model.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed equilibrium conditions, s_mix depends only on composition x through the ideal random-mixing form, with a universal symmetric peak at x=1/2 and fixed endpoint singular structure.
response_change.child_relation: Allow the entropy-composition curve to depend on a sampled environmental input that changes the effective number of accessible local arrangements per species while preserving label symmetry, so the x-to-s_mix mapping remains symmetric but its curvature and peak height vary with that input.
response_change.observable_effect: Across different sampled environmental conditions, the entropy maximum at x=1/2 is reduced or restored and the mid-composition curvature changes, while the parent predicts the same curve for all such conditions.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying the environmental condition changes the height and curvature of the symmetric entropy dome over the same x range; in holdout, the same mechanism persists at unseen condition values, whereas the parent remains condition-independent.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the added environmental effect vanishes and all sites again have the full equivalent local-state accessibility assumed in ideal random mixing.
plan.promotion_reason: The omitted effect is conditional on an external equilibrium setting (for example confinement or finite local degeneracy) that is not encoded by x alone; without one additional sampled input, the target mapping cannot vary across environments.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the same full set of accessible microscopic arrangements for every equilibrium condition, so composition is the only determinant of configurational entropy.
plan.baseline_assumption: All microscopic sites are equivalent and occupancies are statistically independent in a fixed environment with composition-independent local state accessibility.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Environment-dependent reduction of accessible local configurational states, such as confinement or limited orientational degeneracy, modifies the combinatorial entropy without introducing energetic interactions or breaking species-exchange symmetry.
plan.rationale: The parent response relationship is a fixed-environment shortcut: once x is specified, s_mix is fully determined by the ideal binary formula. A realistic next refinement is to relax the assumption that the local configurational state count is unchanged across all equilibrium sampling conditions. Vary an external environmental control (to be added as an input) while holding zero energetic interactions, equilibrium, and species symmetry fixed. Then compare s_mix versus x across at least two admissible values of that control. The parent predicts identical entropy curves for both conditions. The child predicts a changed target mapping itself, not merely auxiliary hidden structure: the symmetric entropy dome is compressed or restored, with altered mid-composition curvature and peak value, most visibly for x near 1/2 and weakly near x≈0 or 1 where mixing entropy already vanishes. This is scientifically admissible when confinement or local degeneracy restrictions modify accessible arrangements but do not induce phase separation or species asymmetry. A single refit of the parent cannot reproduce different entropy-composition curves across those conditions because it has no environmental argument at all. The limitation is that if the sampled environment never varies, this refinement cannot be observed.

contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying x at several fixed confinement_strength values already reveals whether confinement relief is broad or concentrated near x=1/2; in holdout, the same mechanism persists as stronger narrowing of the entropy peak under larger confinement without changing symmetry or positivity.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the sharpened recovery-shape parameter tends to zero or to the value reproducing the current polynomial form.
contract.domain_mechanism: selective cooperative restoration of local configurational accessibility under confinement
contract.scientific_mechanism: Higher-order cooperative accessibility: local rearrangements under confinement require more nearly balanced local species populations than assumed in the parent, sharpening recovery of accessible configurations only near equimolar composition while preserving exchange symmetry and nonnegativity.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the mixedness-dependent confinement relief now has a sharper finite-capacity onset near equimolar composition, changing shoulder curvature and peak narrowing in a way that cannot be reproduced by globally rescaling the original broad polynomial response.
contract.assumption_before: The confinement-induced loss of accessible arrangements is relieved by a low-order polynomial function of mixedness with one broad symmetric composition regime.
contract.assumption_after: Cooperative accessibility recovery is more selective, with effective relief saturating toward appreciable values only when mixedness is very close to its equimolar maximum.
contract.before_fragment: (-x*log(x) - (1 - x)*log(1 - x))/(1 + confinement_strength/(1 + accessibility_scale*(x*(1 - x))**2*(1 + cooperative_accessibility*(x*(1 - x)))))

contract.observable_signature: At fixed accessibility_scale and cooperative_accessibility, scan x across the composition range for several nonzero confinement_strength values. response_change.observable_effect: For the same confinement_strength, the entropy peak stays at x=1/2 but the approach to that peak becomes flatter at intermediate x and sharper close to x=1/2 than the parent can achieve with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when confinement_strength is appreciable and sampled compositions include both intermediate mixtures and near-equimolar mixtures, so that accessibility recovery under restriction is not already negligible; strongest for x away from 0,1 but distinguishable between x(1-x)≈0.1 and x≈0.5.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate confinement already shows symmetric entropy suppression with some recovery around mixed compositions; in holdout at stronger confinement or denser sampling near x=1/2, the sharper late-stage recovery reveals that one smooth recovery phase is insufficient.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the added heterogeneity weight goes to zero or when the second recovery branch collapses onto the first branch's composition scale, eliminating the extra curvature distinction.
plan.gap_statement: The parent assumes a single homogeneous composition-dependent accessibility-recovery phase under confinement, but real restricted environments can contain a more strongly blocked subset of local configurations that becomes accessible only in more nearly equimolar neighborhoods.
plan.baseline_assumption: The process already present—composition-assisted recovery of accessible local arrangements under confinement—is represented by one uniform smooth composition dependence for all restricted microconfigurations.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Heterogeneous confinement relief: different subsets of local configurational states require different degrees of local species balance, producing a two-stage symmetric recovery of entropy with composition rather than one-phase recovery.
plan.rationale: Vary composition x at fixed confinement_strength, with accessibility_scale and cooperative_accessibility fixed. In the parent, the entropy suppression relaxes through one symmetric accessibility function of x(1-x), so after refitting one shared parameter set the curve shape across intermediate and near-equimolar compositions is still constrained to a single-phase recovery. A scientifically admissible refinement is to relax that homogeneity assumption without introducing energetics or breaking species-exchange symmetry: some restricted local arrangements remain inaccessible until the neighborhood is more nearly balanced than the rest. Then the target mapping itself changes, not just auxiliary interpretation: s_mix(x) under confinement has weaker recovery at intermediate x but stronger curvature and a sharper rise near x=1/2, while keeping nonnegativity and the same peak location. This effect is observable when confinement is strong enough that the denominator materially suppresses entropy yet not so extreme that all mixed compositions look equally blocked. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the flatter shoulders and the sharper central recovery across those conditions because it has only one recovery phase tied to one mixedness channel.
